objective: Build the tutor eval suite in evals/ (#10): (1) a frozen case set covering all four key-moment kinds plus hints, generated from move sequences with real Stockfish and detect(); (2) a live runner that asks the real tutor session for each case on a chosen model/effort, with a hard spending cap; (3) deterministic graders for NFR-6 (moves legal in the position, quoted evaluations match this turn's tool results or key-moment data), NFR-7 (the first message and the pre-reveal arrows don't give away the answer), schema/outcome, latency and cost; (4) a report (Markdown + JSON) that compares runs side by side so Q-3 (Opus 5.5 vs Sonnet 5.5) can be decided. All tests use a fake Anthropic client; you never call the real API.
contract:
Decisions (user, 2026-11-08; architecture §5 updated in 15d63a6, read it): live calls, not the Batches API; run locally now; CI gate comes later (coordinator adds the workflow job, it skips without the secret); budget $10 total for #10, so each run takes --max-usd and stops starting new cases once the summed cost reaches it.

How the server builds the tutor (copy this, don't import apps/server): apps/server/src/tutor-setup.ts setupTutor() reads prompts/tutor-system.v1.md, builds createTutorSession({client, engine, explorer, repertoire, config, systemPrompt}, {playerColor, playerProfile: PLAYER_PROFILE}); PLAYER_PROFILE = "Rated around 1000 on Chess.com. Plays the London System as White and the King's Indian Defence as Black." apps/server/src/config.ts loadTutorConfig("development") gives model/effort/maxToolRounds/engine{depth,movetimeCapMs,multiPv}/explorer{ratings,speeds} from config/tutor.json and config/models.json. Repertoire: parseRepertoirePgn + buildRepertoire from @chess-tutor/chess-core over repertoire/*.pgn (see apps/server/src/repertoire.ts). Key-moment requests: { kind:"key_moment", moment, fen: position after the move, attemptFen: position before the move for player_blunder/missed_win else fen, history: UCI including the triggering move }; hints: { kind:"hint", fen, history }. Engine: createWasmEngine/createEngineFromEnv from @chess-tutor/engine (one search at a time). Explorer for evals: a deterministic stub returning unavailable (no network in evals by default); a --live-explorer flag may use the real client if LICHESS_TOKEN is set.

A working prototype of the live harness exists: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-daveharms-personal-workspace-chess-tutor/029814ab-5fb1-4dfa-a9cc-a73999ef0392/scratchpad/model-bakeoff/bakeoff.ts (read it; it wraps client.messages.stream to record each round's stop_reason, tool_use inputs, text and usage, and prices usage). Its 12 real replies (Opus 5.5 medium, Sonnet 5.5 medium, Opus 5.5 low on 4 positions) are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-daveharms-personal-workspace-chess-tutor/029814ab-5fb1-4dfa-a9cc-a73999ef0392/scratchpad/032-evals-r1/bakeoff-results.json: use them as grader test fixtures (copy what you need into evals/test/fixtures/). Known defects in those replies the graders must flag: Sonnet medium hint arrow h7->h7 (degenerate); arrow f1->h7 when revealMove is f1d3 and f4->e5 when revealMove is f4d6 (arrow along the answer move's line = NFR-7 give-away); Opus low punish_opponent message 'can a check with your other bishop make that problem worse' (gives the answer away in words: grade it as a give-away only if your rule catches it deterministically, e.g. names the answer's piece AND the check; otherwise leave it to a future LLM judge and say so). The false 'pins the knight on f6' claim (Trompowsky, e7 blocks the diagonal) is out of reach for deterministic graders: list it in the report as needing a judge; do not build an LLM judge this round.

Cases: evals/cases/*.json, each { id, kind, playerColor, history (UCI), fen, moment|null, attemptFen, engineBest (UCI at attemptFen), source note }. At least 8 per key-moment kind (opponent_left_book, player_blunder, missed_win, punish_opponent) and 8 hints, London as White and KID as Black, typical 1000-level mistakes. A generator script (evals/src/generate-cases.ts) plays SAN sequences listed in evals/cases/sequences.json through real Stockfish (config engine depth/movetime) and detect() with config thresholds and the repertoire, and writes the case files; a sequence that does not produce its intended kind is reported and skipped. Commit the generated cases (they freeze the engine data).

Graders (independent of packages/tutor internals: its package exports only '.'; implement with chess.js): moves named in message/reveal (SAN incl. castling/promotion, UCI, long algebraic) legal in the case's fen or attemptFen or a position from the case history; revealMove legal at attemptFen and equal to or within config tutor.attemptToleranceCp of engineBest (compute with the engine during the run or record cp_loss); quoted evaluations (+N.N, N.N pawns, N cp, mate in N) match a score in this case's tool results (from the recorded rounds) or the key-moment data, sign-aware where the text names a side; NFR-7: message does not name revealMove in any notation, no pre-reveal arrow equals revealMove, starts at its from-square, ends at its to-square, or runs along its line through the to-square; arrows well-formed (distinct real squares, <= 3). Outcome ok/reason, tool calls used, latency (total, first API round), cost.

Runner CLI: pnpm eval -- --model <id> --effort <level> [--cases <glob|kind>] [--max-usd N] [--concurrency N default 2] [--repeat N] --out <dir default evals/results/<timestamp>-<model>-<effort>>. Writes per-case JSON (full recorded rounds) + summary.json + report.md. A compare command (pnpm eval -- compare <dir> <dir> ...) writes a side-by-side report: NFR-6 move legality %, eval-match %, NFR-7 no-give-away % (target >= 90), ok rate and failure reasons, latency p50/p95, cost per case and per game (assume 10 key moments per game), with per-case rows. Prices from config/models.json pricingPerMTok (cache writes 1.25x input).
